Title II, ACC-HHS-TITLE-II-TOTAL -- printed as 'Total, Title II, Department of Health and Human Services' 1,300,549,900 [FY 2025 Estimate], PDF p.365 (printed p.361). Source: H.Rept. 119-271's 'FY 2025 Estimate' column, which the report defines (pp.319-320) as 'FY 2025 Operating Plans and other available information'; FY2025 was a full-year continuing resolution (P.L. 119-4, Full-Year Continuing Appropriations Act, 2025, division A). P.L. 119-4 sec. 1109(a): amounts necessary to maintain program levels -- no dollar level in law; this is the report's estimate. Parts the law does set: P.L. 119-4 sec. 1908(2), 139 Stat. 33: HRSA-Wide Activities and Program Support, '"$0" for "$890,788,000"' (with $219,588,000 for $1,110,376,000); P.L. 119-4 sec. 1908(3), 139 Stat. 33: SAMHSA Health Surveillance and Program Support, '"$0" for "$72,090,000"'; P.L. 119-4 sec. 1908(4), 139 Stat. 33: ACF Children and Families Services Programs, '"$0" for "$40,011,000"'; P.L. 119-4 sec. 1908(5), 139 Stat. 33: ACL Aging and Disability Services Programs, '"$0" for "$29,268,000"'; P.L. 119-4 sec. 1902(b), 139 Stat. 31: HCFAC level '$941,000,000' (+24,000 +1,000 +1,000 over Div. D); P.L. 119-4 sec. 1101(a)(8), 139 Stat. 11: Div. D sec. 240 continued 'by substituting "$1,471,000,000" for "$1,250,000,000"'; P.L. 119-4 sec. 1109(b)(2), 139 Stat. 13: Medicaid advance for 1st quarter FY2026 '$261,063,820,000'. H.Rept. 119-271 counts the HHS rescissions (Nonrecurring Expenses Fund) inside Title II (House scope), unlike the FY2024 figures recorded from S.Rept. 118-207.

Title II, ACC-HHS-TITLE-II-TOTAL -- printed as 'Total, Title II, Department of Health and Human Services discretionary' 114,965,801 [FY 2025 Estimate], PDF p.366 (printed p.362). Source: H.Rept. 119-271's 'FY 2025 Estimate' column, which the report defines (pp.319-320) as 'FY 2025 Operating Plans and other available information'; FY2025 was a full-year continuing resolution (P.L. 119-4, Full-Year Continuing Appropriations Act, 2025, division A). Equals the P.L. 119-4 level in the House scope: Scope only: B - A = -1,471,000 is exactly the FY2025 NEF rescission, which H.Rept. 119-271 counts inside Title II (House scope) and the S.Rept. 118-207 FY2024 baseline leaves out (Senate scope). In the House scope (FY2024 116,122,958) A = 116,122,958 - 1,006,157 - 221,000 (NEF increase) + 70,000 (Adoption Incentives excluded) = 114,965,801 = B. CURES is outside the Title II totals. H.Rept. 119-271 counts the HHS rescissions (Nonrecurring Expenses Fund) inside Title II (House scope), unlike the FY2024 figures recorded from S.Rept. 118-207.

account.canonical_name: Title II, Department of Health and Human Services (title total)
account.notes: Derived rollup -- the Title II title total as printed. Reconciles as the ten agency totals (eleven in the FY2026-27 requests, with AHA) + General Provisions lines (signed) - the CURES Act line, in all 16 printed columns (reference/review/lhhs/title_ii_totals.py); in the store, through the agency-total rollups and the four General Provisions accounts, in all 13 recorded cells. The House counts the HHS rescissions (NEF, Adoption Incentives) in Title II's general provisions; the Senate prints them after the grand total, outside Title II -- so the two FY2024 figures differ by 1,320,000 as printed.
